summary: Most material claims verify against primary sources: CareScout 2025 TX AL median $5,666 (private one-bedroom), all six BLS OEWS 2025 Texas wages (O*NET), §553.47 fees ($300+$15/bed, cap $2,250, late fee, $15/bed capacity, $300 Alzheimer's), §553.21/§553.23 timelines (30-day review, 30-day issuance, 120-day denials, 1-3 residents after LSC), §553.253 staffing (Type B awake night staff regardless of size, attendant always present, manager 40 hrs, training hours), §553.5 types, §553.225 sprinkler/alarm rules, §553.17 floodplain and 5-year look-back, HRC §§123.004/.006/.008, STAR+PLUS Handbook §7200 setting rules, room & board $994-$85=$909, TWC 2.70%/$9,000, franchise threshold $2.65M, NIC 88.4%, HUD SAFMR $3,190, Census, NCAL fact sheet, all HHSC phone numbers/emails/regional directors, medication aide permit details, proposed rule 25R031, and the $13.00 attendant wage. Model recompute matches the narrative (40-unit +$59,004; 16-bed private +$24,655; 16-bed mixed +$8,121; 6-bed private +$2,480; 6-bed mixed -$3,031). Main problems: (1) the 40-unit apartment building's rent is a per-bed house rent and is understated by ~$41k/month, which cuts the top-ranked configuration from +$59k to ~+$17.9k/month and changes the ranking; (2) the 6-bed homes have no nurse even though PL 2023-22 requires a nurse for medication administration; (3) STAR+PLUS levels are described as RUG-based though the 9/1/2025 T2031 codes come from PDPM and phase in at ISP renewal. The S20 STAR+PLUS rate PDF could not be retrieved (HTTP 403), so the 18 T2031 amounts remain unverified, not disproven.

issues.evidence: The 40-unit lease is the Dallas 4-bedroom HOUSE SAFMR ($3,190) x1.15 / 6 beds = $611.50, multiplied by 40. But this configuration is explicitly built with STAR+PLUS 'apartment' units, which the STAR+PLUS Handbook §7200 says need 'a private bath and cooking facilities, including a kitchen with a sink, refrigerator' and at least 220 sq ft single occupancy. A unit with its own bath and kitchen is at minimum a studio apartment; the same cited source page (S41, ZIP 75287) lists the FY2027 studio SAFMR at $1,640/month, so 40 units = $65,600/month before any common areas (dining, kitchen, activity space, offices). Recomputing the model with $65,600 drops typeB40_mixed from +$59,004/month to +$17,864/month at 88% (conservative 80%: +$3,789; break-even occupancy 0.545 -> 0.778) and it falls from #1 to #2 behind typeB16_private. The executive summary's '$59,000/month' headline and the financial_narrative results table are therefore overstated.
issues.fix: Set the typeB40_mixed lease override to at least 65600 (40 x FY2027 studio SAFMR $1,640 for ZIP 75287 [S41]; also cite STAR+PLUS Handbook §7200 [S21] for the private bath/kitchen unit requirement), label it an operator estimate floor that excludes common areas, update startup 'Lease deposit + first month' high to 131200, and update executive_summary, financial_narrative results table and sensitivity to the recomputed values (~+$17,900/month at 88%, ~+$3,800 at 80%, break-even ~78%).

issues.current: Attendant 24/7 + manager only; no licensed nurse or RN line
issues.correct: Add an on-call/consulting nurse line, e.g. LVN 17.3 hrs/month (4 hrs/week) at $29.92 [S32], operator estimate
issues.evidence: HHSC's April 17, 2024 ALF webinar (PL 2023-22) says only a 'Licensed nurse employed/contracted by the ALF', a permitted medication aide who 'acts under authority of a nurse on duty or on call by the facility', or an 'ALF attendant to whom an RN has delegated medication administration' may administer medications. The 16- and 40-bed configs include an LVN for this reason, but the 6-bed configs have no nurse at all, so they cannot legally administer medications to residents who need it. Adding 4 hrs/week LVN cuts typeB6_private from +$2,480 to +$1,876 at 88% and to -$486 at 80% (break-even 0.796 -> 0.816); typeB6_mixed from -$3,031 to -$3,635.
issues.fix: Add to both 6-bed configurations: {"role": "LVN/RN on call - medication aide supervision or RN delegation, service plan reviews (4 hrs/week)", "basis": "hours_per_month", "amount": 17.3, "wage_hourly": 29.92, "wage_source_id": "S32", "cite": "PL 2023-22", "notes": "Hours are an operator estimate - verify locally."} (or state that the home will only admit residents who self-administer), and update the 6-bed figures in executive_summary, financial_narrative, risks and corrections_vs_previous.

issues.current: Levels map to RUG/HCBS groups listed on the rate sheet
issues.correct: T2031 levels come from the PDPM-based methodology that replaced RUG-III on 9/1/2025; providers keep billing the old RUG-III codes for a member until that member's ISP renews, then switch to T2031
issues.evidence: UnitedHealthcare provider notice: assisted living claims for STAR+PLUS members must switch to HCPCS T2031 and modifiers following Texas's move 'from the RUG-III payment model to the patient-driven payment model (PDPM)'. The methodology changed Sept. 1, 2025, but providers 'keep using the current RUG-III codes until a member's individual service plan (ISP) renews'; claims with the wrong codes are denied.
issues.fix: Replace 'RUG/HCBS group' with 'PDPM-based level (replaced RUG-III 9/1/2025)' in the T2031 rate notes and the reimbursement section, and add a checklist/billing note that T2031 codes apply only from each member's next ISP renewal on or after 9/1/2025 (cite the UHC notice or HHSC's provider guide as a new source).
